current_question_summary: 8 trees (mango, guava, papaya, pomegranate, lemon, banana, raspberry, apple) in two rows of 4, North/South facing. Lemon between mango & apple, opposite guava; banana at a row-end, immediately right of guava; raspberry at a row-end, diagonally opposite mango. Question: "Which of the following statements is definitely true?" Options: A) Papaya next to apple, B) Apple next to lemon, C) Raspberry left of or after Pomegranate, D) Pomegranate diagonally opposite banana. Marked correct: D.
your_independent_calculation: Let guava's row = X, other row = Y. Banana=X4 (row-end, immediately right of guava => guava=X3). Lemon=Y3 (directly opposite guava). Lemon between mango & apple => {mango,apple} = {Y2,Y4} (they flank lemon). Since lemon is 'between' mango and apple by definition, apple (whichever of Y2/Y4 it is) is ALWAYS immediately adjacent to lemon (Y3) -- this makes option B unconditionally, definitely true regardless of any further ambiguity. Separately, raspberry (a row-end) being diagonally opposite mango pins raspberry at X1, leaving papaya/pomegranate to fill the two remaining leftover cells (Y1 and X2) -- NOT uniquely determined by the clues (independently confirmed by companion sub-question id 8946c2b7 in the same puzzle set, whose own stored/verified answer is 'Papaya or Pomegranate', i.e. ambiguous). Banana's diagonal partner (X4's diagonal) is Y3=lemon under the chessboard-shift diagonal convention (validated elsewhere in this batch via the flats puzzle), or Y1 (papaya-or-pomegranate, ambiguous) under a corner-to-corner convention -- under NEITHER convention is pomegranate 'definitely' diagonally opposite banana. So D is not definitely true, while B is definitely true.
recommended_fix: Change correct_answer from D to B ("Apple tree is just next to lemon tree"). Rewrite explanation to note this follows directly and unconditionally from clue 1 (lemon is between mango and apple, so apple must be adjacent to lemon), and that option D is unproven/false since banana's opposite-row diagonal cell is never necessarily pomegranate.
notes: Cross-validated using companion sub-question id 8946c2b7 in the same puzzle set (same base clues), which independently corroborates the derived cell layout used here.

current_question_summary: Same 8-tree puzzle as above. Question: "Which tree is just opposite to banana tree?" Options: A) Mango, B) Pomegranate, C) Papaya, D) Data is inadequate. Marked correct: B (Pomegranate).
your_independent_calculation: As derived for the companion question above: banana sits at the end of guava's row (X4); lemon sits directly opposite guava (Y3); mango and apple flank lemon at Y2 and Y4. The cell directly opposite banana (X4) is Y4, which is ALWAYS occupied by mango or apple (never by pomegranate -- pomegranate/papaya only ever fill the two other leftover cells, Y1 and X2). So 'pomegranate' can never be the tree opposite banana; this is a structural certainty independent of diagonal-convention ambiguity. Given the option set offers 'Mango' (not 'Apple'), and the companion 'definitely true' question in this same set (id 162523fb, also flagged) is only consistent when mango occupies Y4 under a corner-to-corner diagonal convention, the best-supported correct answer here is 'Mango' (option A).
recommended_fix: Change correct_answer from B to A (Mango). Rewrite explanation: the cell directly opposite banana is occupied by mango (one of the two trees flanking lemon), not pomegranate.
notes: That the answer cannot be 'Pomegranate' is very high confidence (structural/positional impossibility). The specific replacement 'Mango' (vs. a possible 'Mango or Apple' framing) carries more residual uncertainty since it depends on which diagonal convention the original source intended, but Mango is the best-supported single answer given the options offered.

current_question_summary: Two cars start 150 km apart on a road, moving toward each other. your_independent_calculation: Car 1's right-then-left detour (15 km off-road, 25 km back parallel to the road, then a leg back onto the road) nets 25+25 = 50 km of along-road progress once it 'reaches the main road' again (sideways offset cancels, as stated in the problem). Car 2 has advanced 35 km along the road. Remaining gap = 150 - (50 + 35) = 150 - 85 = 65 km, matching option A exactly.

current_question_summary: Radha moves South-East 7 km, then West 14 km, then North-West 7 km, then East 4 km. Find distance from starting point. Options: A) 3 km, B) 4 km, C) 10 km, D) 11 km. Marked correct: B (4 km).

current_question_summary: One morning, Udai and Vishal talk face to face at a crossing. Vishal's shadow falls exactly to Udai's left. Which direction is Udai facing? Options: A) East, B) West, C) North, D) South. Marked correct: A (East).
your_independent_calculation: Morning sun rises in the East, so all shadows point West (a fixed compass direction, independent of anyone's body orientation). Vishal's shadow (pointing West) falls to Udai's LEFT side. For a person facing compass bearing theta, their left-hand direction is (theta - 90) mod 360. Setting left = West (270 deg): theta - 90 = 270 => theta = 360 = 0 deg = North. So Udai faces North. Cross-checked against 3 structurally identical shadow/direction questions elsewhere in this same batch (ids 31156324 Vimal/Stephen, ec66b0f8 Suresh/pole, 8993c7cd Rekha/Hema), all of which are internally consistent and independently verified correct using this same left/right-facing formula -- confirming the method is right and this question is the outlier.
recommended_fix: Change correct_answer from A to C (North).
notes: The stored explanation itself visibly struggles and self-contradicts (marks its own reasoning attempts with '✗' twice, then simply asserts 'Standard answer: Udai faces East' without a valid derivation) -- consistent with the same data/generation bug pattern found in 4 other flagged questions in this batch.

The stored explanation itself computes 34347 but then hand-waves it as '≈ 34357 (rounding in question)', which is not a valid rounding (the arithmetic is exact, no fractional remainder). The final answer, Option A (2 years), is unaffected.
notes: Answer choice itself is fine; only the numeric value stated in the question/explanation is off by Rs.10 from the true CI at n=2.

This same median formula is used correctly elsewhere in this very batch (e.g. id 2c88bb55/mango-yield median=66 checks out), confirming the method, so the 111.6 result should be trusted over the stated 120.

The question needs a corrected option set with ~Rs.112 as the median value (keeping whichever '183 workers' or similar reading for part ii, which is a graph-reading figure not independently verifiable here). At minimum, correct the explanation's median-formula line, which currently jumps from '110 + 1.6' logic to an unexplained final claim of '~120' that contradicts its own numbers.
